response: The familial transmission of drinking patterns does exhibit some persistence into young adulthood, but the relationship is non-linear. Changes in the lower part of the familial drinking distribution are strongly related to drinking in young adults. However, the actual levels of drinking in drinking families appear less important in shaping the drinking patterns of the offspring in young adulthood. This suggests that while family influences can play a role in shaping drinking behaviors, their impact may be more nuanced and complex than a direct, linear transmission of drinking patterns.
